perspective:
Jose Castillo’s available information:

- He works with Patricia Ndiaye at a community bank, where he occasionally helps with maintenance and repairs.
- They have a friendly, professional relationship and normally talk about everyday work experiences.
- He remembers Patricia as usually vibrant, so he notices when she seems more withdrawn than usual.
- He asks if she’s okay; she says it’s “nothing really,” just “personal stuff,” and thanks him for asking.
- He offers to listen if she ever wants to talk; she says she appreciates it.
- He overhears her on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- He brings up financial planning and offers to discuss budgeting tips; Patricia says she’s been overwhelmed with bills and will take him up on the offer soon.
- He worries afterward that he may have overstepped, so he tells her he only wanted to help, not pry.
- Patricia reassures him she didn’t think he was prying and is grateful for his help.
- He tells her he respects her privacy and wants to support her as a friend; she appreciates that.
- He senses she appreciates his concern but seems to prefer handling her personal issues privately.
- He checks in with her later; Patricia says she’s fine and planning a quiet weekend at home.
- He continues offering support, including just grabbing coffee; Patricia says she’s busy but handling things and is grateful for his support.
- He tells her he’s there anytime and that they’re all there to help each other.
